top_temples.name: Chandaneswar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Near the Odisha-West Bengal border, Balasore district; major pilgrimage site during the Chaitra Mela festival.

top_temples.name: Panchalingeswar Temple
top_temples.location_note: In the Nilagiri Hills, Balasore district; distinctive for five naturally occurring Shiva lingams under a perpetual stream.

top_temples.name: Khirachora Gopinath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Balasore district; a centuries-old Vaishnavite shrine associated with visits from Chaitanya Mahaprabhu.

top_temples.name: Nilagiri Jagannath Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the foothills of Swarnachuda Hill in Nilagiri, about 17 km from Balasore town; the district's second most prominent Jagannath shrine.

top_temples.name: Bhudhara Chandi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Balasore; built by King Basanta Bhujanga Mandhata of the Ganga dynasty.

top_temples.name: Nrusinghanath Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the foothills of Gandhamardhan Hill near Paikmal, Bargarh district; dates to 1413 AD, Kalinga-style architecture.

top_temples.name: Budharaja Temple
top_temples.location_note: At the foot of Papanga Hill in Bargarh, alongside a forest garden and a Ram temple.

top_temples.name: Tara Tarini Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 35 km from Berhampur atop a hill reached via 999 steps; a major Shakti Peetha of Odisha.

top_temples.name: Sri Sri Sidhi Binayak Pitha
top_temples.location_note: Giri Road, Berhampur; among the largest Ganesha temples in Odisha, gold-toned exterior.

top_temples.name: Maa Budi Thakurani Temple
top_temples.location_note: Old town Big Bazaar, Berhampur; regarded as the city's Ista Devi (presiding deity).

top_temples.name: Mahuri Kalua Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the highway connecting Berhampur to Western Odisha, in the Kerandi hills forest range.

top_temples.name: Narayani Devi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Along the Eastern Ghats mountain ranges near Berhampur.

top_temples.name: Lingaraj Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bhubaneswar's largest and most famous temple; 64 subsidiary shrines and a 180-m spire, the city's defining shrine as the 'Temple City of India'.

top_temples.name: Parashurameshvara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bhubaneswar; the oldest surviving temple in the city, dated to the 7th-8th century CE.

top_temples.name: Mukteshvara Temple
top_temples.location_note: Bhubaneswar; 10th-century, called the 'Gem of Odishan Architecture' for its Kalinga-style carvings.

top_temples.name: Rajarani Temple
top_temples.deity: Shiva (no presiding idol; devoted to worship)
top_temples.location_note: Bhubaneswar; built 11th-12th century, famed for sandstone architecture and sculptural work.

top_temples.name: Brahma Temple (Vaital Deul complex area)
top_temples.location_note: Bhubaneswar; foundation laid by 15th-century Gajapati rulers, iconic Kalinga architectural style.

top_temples.name: Cuttack Chandi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Near the Mahanadi river in Cuttack; presiding deity of the city, major Durga Puja celebrations.

top_temples.name: Bhattarika Temple
top_temples.location_note: Atop a small hill amid the Mahanadi river near Cuttack; associated with the legend of Parashurama.

top_temples.name: Charchika Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of Cuttack's oldest temples, dedicated to an eight-armed form of the goddess.

top_temples.name: Dhabaleswar Temple
top_temples.location_note: On an island in the Mahanadi River near Cuttack, reached by boat or hanging bridge.

top_temples.name: Singhanatha Temple
top_temples.location_note: One of the earliest temples in Odisha, near Cuttack, noted for rare artwork.

top_temples.name: Maa Biraja Temple
top_temples.deity: Durga (as Biraja/Girija), with Shiva as Jagannath
top_temples.location_note: Jajpur's central shrine, about 125 km north of Bhubaneswar; one of the major Maha Shakti Peethas of India.

top_temples.name: Siddheshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Jajpur district; one of the oldest Shiva temples in the area, near a notable Ganesh shrine.

top_temples.name: Ramchandi Temple
top_temples.location_note: In a cave about 10 km from Jharsuguda town; a recognized Shakti Peetha of Odisha.

top_temples.name: Jhadeswar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Jharsuguda; a well-known local Shiva shrine.

top_temples.name: Pahadi Mandir (Pahadeswar Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Atop a small hill about 2 km from Jharsuguda bus stand; major Mahashivratri celebrations.

top_temples.name: Maheswari Temple
top_temples.location_note: Jharsuguda district.

top_temples.name: Kanak Durga Mandir
top_temples.location_note: Jharsuguda district; a well-known local Devi shrine.

top_temples.name: Konark Sun Temple
top_temples.location_note: Odisha's only UNESCO World Heritage Site; built mid-13th century by Narasingha Deva I, designed as a monumental chariot of the sun god.

top_temples.name: Ramchandi Temple, Konark
top_temples.location_note: About 10 km from Konark town on Ramchandi Beach, at the mouth of the Kushabhadra River; a distinct shrine from Konark's main Sun Temple.

top_temples.name: Nilamadhaba Temple, Kantilo
top_temples.location_note: Kantilo, about 34 km from Nayagarh town; legend holds this as where Lord Jagannath was first worshipped by tribal chief Biswabasu.

top_temples.name: Ladukeswar Temple (Ladubaba)
top_temples.location_note: Nayagarh town; draws large crowds during Shivratri, one of the district's most popular shrines.

top_temples.name: Jagannath Temple
top_temples.deity: Jagannath (Vishnu form), with Balabhadra and Subhadra
top_temples.location_note: Puri's defining shrine, one of the Char Dham pilgrimage sites; famous for the annual Rath Yatra.

top_temples.name: Vimala Temple
top_temples.location_note: Within the Jagannath Temple complex in Puri; a Shakti Peetha, traditionally visited before offerings at the main shrine.

top_temples.name: Lokanath Temple
top_temples.location_note: Puri; legend attributes its establishment to Lord Rama, one of the five major Shiva temples in the city.

top_temples.name: Markandeshwar Temple
top_temples.location_note: Puri; dates to the 13th century, one of the 52 sacred Shiva worship sites in the region.

top_temples.name: Varahi Temple
top_temples.location_note: Puri; a distinctive Shakti shrine depicting the goddess Varahi.

top_temples.name: Vedvyas Temple
top_temples.location_note: Rourkela; one of the city's most significant religious sites, dedicated to the compiler of the Vedas and the Mahabharata.

top_temples.name: Hanuman Vatika
top_temples.location_note: Rourkela; features a 75-ft Hanuman statue, one of Asia's tallest, inaugurated 1994.

top_temples.name: Laxmi Narayan Temple
top_temples.location_note: Rourkela city.

top_temples.name: Maa Tarini Temple
top_temples.location_note: About 9 km from downtown Rourkela; established 1969, presiding deity for local devotees.

top_temples.name: Santoshi Maa Temple
top_temples.location_note: Rourkela; known for its distinctive pink-hued architecture.

top_temples.name: Maa Samaleswari Temple
top_temples.location_note: On the bank of the Mahanadi, about 3 km from Sambalpur town; presiding deity of the city, gives Sambalpur its name and identity.

top_temples.name: Budharaja Temple, Sambalpur
top_temples.location_note: Atop Budharaja hill in Sambalpur; a well-known city landmark.

top_temples.name: Leaning Temple of Huma (Bimaleswar Temple)
top_temples.location_note: Huma village, about 23 km south of Sambalpur on the Mahanadi; a rare 17th-century temple that leans at 13.8 degrees, one of only two leaning temples in the world.

top_temples.name: Anokha Shree Shyam Bihari Mandir
top_temples.location_note: A large temple within Sambalpur city.

top_temples.name: Shirdi Sai Temple, Sambalpur
top_temples.location_note: Sambalpur city; a popular meditation and worship spot.
